--- axis-min-max-nullable ---
fix(type): add missing nullable type for the axis `min` and `max` option
## Context TypeScript users can return `null` or `undefined` from axis `min` and `max` callbacks at runtime, but the current type declarations incorrectly reject that documented pattern. ## Desired outcome The type surface for axis `min` and `max` should allow nullable callback results so the declarations match the supported API. ## Acceptance signals Axis configurations whose `min` or `max` callbacks return `null` or `undefined` pass type-checking without changing the existing runtime behavior.
--- axislabel-formatter-index ---
feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`
## Context Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly. ## Desired outcome `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`. ## Acceptance signals A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.
--- axislabel-formatter-indexing ---
fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter
## Context A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly. ## Desired outcome When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position. ## Acceptance signals For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.
--- bar-zero-size-labels ---
fix(bar): fix wrong label position when bar width/height is 0
## Context Bar labels can end up on the wrong side when a bar’s width or height is zero, which is especially visible in sparse or collapsed datasets where labels matter most. ## Desired outcome Zero-size bars should still place outside labels according to the intended axis direction and inversion rules rather than falling back to a misleading default side. ## Acceptance signals Bars with zero width or height keep their labels on the correct visual side instead of jumping to an obviously wrong position.
--- candlestick-series-encode-render ---
fix(candlestick): fix candlestick render error with `series.encode`
## Context Candlestick charts can render incorrectly or fail outright when data is mapped through `series.encode`, particularly in layouts that are not the simplest default case. ## Desired outcome Candlestick rendering should honor `series.encode` correctly across supported layouts so encoded dimensions still produce a valid candlestick chart. ## Acceptance signals A candlestick series driven by `series.encode` renders with the expected orientation and geometry instead of crashing or misplacing the candle bodies and whiskers.
--- cartesian-small-number-rounding ---
Fix that extreme small numbers can not be displayed in Cartesian due to the inappropriate rounding precision.
## Context Extremely small numeric values can disappear or produce broken tick spacing on Cartesian charts because rounding precision removes information that still matters at the displayed scale. ## Desired outcome Axis extent and tick calculation should preserve enough precision for extremely small numbers across interval, time, and log handling so those data points remain visible. ## Acceptance signals Charts built from very small values still render meaningful extents and ticks instead of collapsing the axis or rounding the data away.
--- chord-export-entry ---
fix(chord): add missing export entry for chord chart
## Context Developers trying to use the chord chart from the packaged library are missing the expected export entry, which makes the feature look unavailable even though the implementation exists. ## Desired outcome The published package should expose the chord chart through the expected chart entry so consumers can import and register it normally. ## Acceptance signals Using the packaged chord chart entry no longer fails because of a missing export, and the chart can be imported the same way as other supported chart types.
--- darkmode-lightness-algorithm ---
fix(theme): adjust dark mode color lightness algorithm
## Context The current dark-mode token lightness adjustment does not create enough contrast between related colors, so charts can look flat and adjacent visual states are harder to read than they should be. ## Desired outcome Dark-theme color derivation should preserve a stronger lightness contrast so derived colors remain distinguishable while still feeling like part of the same palette. ## Acceptance signals In dark mode, related colors keep a clearer visual hierarchy and no longer collapse into nearly identical shades.
--- datazoom-single-point-position ---
fix(dataZoom): fix wrong position of the dataZoom when the series has only one data point
## Context When a chart has only one data point, the slider dataZoom can compute the wrong position and render in the wrong place, which makes simple charts look broken. ## Desired outcome Slider dataZoom should place itself correctly even when the controlled series contains just a single point. ## Acceptance signals A one-point chart shows the dataZoom in the expected location instead of offsetting it because of invalid geometry calculations.
--- gauge-progress-auto-color ---
feat(gauge): `progress.color` supports `'auto'`
## Context Gauge authors can already let some visuals inherit the series color automatically, but progress arcs still require manual color duplication, which makes themed gauges harder to maintain. ## Desired outcome Gauge progress should accept `progress.color: 'auto'` so the progress fill can follow the series color mapping automatically. ## Acceptance signals When `progress.color` is set to `'auto'`, the gauge progress arc adopts the expected automatic color instead of requiring an explicit hard-coded fill.
--- graph-nodescaleratio-type ---
fix(type): fix `nodeScaleRatio` option type for graph series
## Context The TypeScript declaration for graph `nodeScaleRatio` is narrower than the runtime behavior, so valid numeric configurations appear illegal in editors and build checks. ## Desired outcome The public type for `nodeScaleRatio` should accept the numeric values the runtime already supports rather than implying a single fixed literal. ## Acceptance signals Developers can provide ordinary numeric `nodeScaleRatio` values without TypeScript errors, and the runtime behavior remains unchanged.
--- jitter-overlap-avoidance ---
fix(jitter): fix overlap when there is enough space to avoid
## Context Chart authors using scatter jitter are still seeing points overlap even when there is enough open space within the allowed jitter band, which makes dense plots look incorrect and undermines the point of enabling jitter in the first place. ## Desired outcome When overlap avoidance is enabled, the jitter placement should consistently choose a non-overlapping position whenever a valid position exists inside the permitted movement range, and it should only fall back when the available space is genuinely exhausted. ## Acceptance signals A scatter plot with nearby points no longer leaves avoidable collisions behind, and the adjusted points stay within the same jitter budget instead of jumping randomly while free space still exists.
--- js-yaml-3-14-2 ---
chore(deps-dev): bump js-yaml from 3.14.0 to 3.14.2
## Context The development toolchain depends on `js-yaml`, and the repository needs the newer 3.14.2 patch level to keep maintenance dependencies current without changing chart behavior. ## Desired outcome Update the pinned development dependency from `js-yaml` 3.14.0 to 3.14.2 while keeping all runtime chart features and public APIs unchanged. ## Acceptance signals Contributors install the refreshed dev dependency set successfully, and no user-facing ECharts behavior changes as part of the version bump.
--- label-layout-margin ---
Fix/label layout margin
## Context Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates. ## Desired outcome Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments. ## Acceptance signals Labels keep the intended spacing, pie labels and shared axis labels no longer drift because of inconsistent margin math, and overlap prevention reflects the final rendered label geometry.
--- labelline-smooth-reset ---
fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset
## Context Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration. ## Desired outcome Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing. ## Acceptance signals After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.
--- license-headers-precommit ---
chore: add license headers and a script of pre-commit
## Context Contributors currently have no consistent safeguard for Apache license headers, so missing headers can slip into the repository and only get noticed late in review. ## Desired outcome Add repository tooling that checks for required license headers before commit, including a `checkheader` workflow that surfaces missing headers clearly while leaving runtime chart behavior unchanged. ## Acceptance signals Contributors get an actionable pre-commit failure when a required header is missing, and maintainers can enforce header compliance without changing user-facing chart features.
--- line-areastyle-empty-dimension ---
fix(line): fix areaStyle render error when dimension name is empty string
## Context Line series with `areaStyle` can throw a render error when a dataset uses an empty string as a dimension name, even though that data shape should still be renderable. ## Desired outcome Area rendering should tolerate empty-string dimension names instead of treating them as a fatal path through the line-series logic. ## Acceptance signals A line chart with `areaStyle` and a dataset dimension named `''` renders normally instead of failing during area generation.
--- lines-loop-symbol-flip ---
fix(lines): fix effect symbol flip on unidirectional loop end when `roundTrip` is not enabled
## Context Animated symbols on one-way looping `lines` series can briefly flip direction when they cross the loop endpoint, which makes the motion look glitchy even though the route itself is correct. ## Desired outcome When `roundTrip` is not enabled, the effect symbol should preserve a consistent forward orientation across the loop boundary instead of flipping at the turnaround point. ## Acceptance signals A unidirectional looping line animation remains visually continuous, with the effect symbol keeping the expected orientation as it passes the loop end.
--- lint-changed-files-pattern ---
fix(workflow): fix match pattern for changed files collection in the lint action
## Context The lint workflow is missing some changed TypeScript files because the diff pattern does not catch files placed directly under the source root, reducing confidence in CI coverage. ## Desired outcome Update the changed-file matching so linting includes the intended TypeScript files under the source tree, while leaving product behavior untouched. ## Acceptance signals A pull request that changes a matching source-root TypeScript file now triggers the expected lint coverage instead of slipping past the workflow.
--- logscale-negative-exponent-rounding ---
fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent.
## Context Log-scale charts with values that use very large negative exponents can still hit incorrect rounding paths, leading to unstable tick generation and misleading axis output. ## Desired outcome Log-scale rounding should handle extremely small values consistently so charts with tiny magnitudes remain numerically correct and readable. ## Acceptance signals A log axis fed with very small values no longer mis-rounds its scale, and the resulting ticks and labels stay stable across the supported exponent range.
--- marker-z-option ---
feat(marker): markPoint markLine markArea support z option
## Context Chart authors can control stacking depth for many series elements, but marker overlays still lack the same control, which makes it difficult to layer annotations correctly over complex charts. ## Desired outcome `markPoint`, `markLine`, and `markArea` should accept a `z` option so authors can place marker overlays at the intended rendering depth without relying on brittle layering hacks. ## Acceptance signals When a marker is given an explicit `z`, it renders above or below neighboring content in the same predictable way users expect from other chart elements.
--- matrix-darkmode-colors ---
fix(matrix): fix darkMode color
## Context Matrix charts in dark mode still use colors that were tuned for light backgrounds, so borders and structural surfaces can become hard to distinguish and the component looks visually broken next to the rest of the dark theme. ## Desired outcome The dark theme should provide matrix-specific colors that keep the matrix body, dividers, and borders legible and visually balanced on dark backgrounds. ## Acceptance signals A matrix rendered with dark mode shows clear separation between cells and surrounding structure, without washed-out or light-theme border colors leaking through.
--- matrix-dimension-length ---
feat(matrix): support matrix.x/y.length for conveniently creating a headless matrix without composing an array
## Context Creating a headless matrix currently requires authors to build explicit coordinate arrays even when they only know the desired matrix dimensions, which adds unnecessary setup overhead. ## Desired outcome Matrix definitions should allow `matrix.x.length` and `matrix.y.length` so users can declare the size of a headless matrix directly without composing placeholder arrays. ## Acceptance signals A matrix configured only with dimension lengths produces the expected headless grid structure, while existing array-based matrix definitions continue to work.
--- matrix-label-api ---
Fix matrix label API
## Context Matrix users are seeing inconsistent label behavior because matrix labels do not reliably inherit shared text defaults, and coordinate locator ranges can become invalid in edge cases. ## Desired outcome Matrix labels should inherit `option.textStyle` the same way other labels do, and matrix coordinate lookup should handle invalid locator ranges predictably, including the `coordClamp` path instead of producing unusable results. ## Acceptance signals Matrix labels pick up the expected default text styling, and matrix coordinate calculations no longer fail or return confusing ranges when some locator values are missing or out of bounds.
--- matrix-label-formatter ---
fix(matrix): fix matrix label formatter does not work
## Context Matrix users can declare label formatters, but those formatters are not actually being applied, which makes matrix labels ignore both template strings and callback-based formatting logic. ## Desired outcome Matrix labels should honor `label.formatter` consistently, including string templates and function formatters, and formatter callbacks should receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`. ## Acceptance signals A matrix label configured with either formatter style renders the formatted text rather than the raw value, and callback formatters receive the documented data they need.
--- notice-year-2026 ---
chore: update NOTICE year to 2026
## Context The project is entering the 2026 release cycle, and Apache distribution artifacts need their bundled notice text to reflect the current copyright year. This is not a charting behavior change, but it is part of the published package and should stay accurate for downstream users and redistributors. ## Desired outcome Update the shipped notice so it states the Apache ECharts copyright range through 2026. This is a maintenance-only change in a user-facing distribution file rather than a product feature request. ## Acceptance signals The distributed NOTICE text reads `Copyright 2017-2026 The Apache Software Foundation`. No other package contents, runtime behavior, API contracts, or chart rendering behavior should change.
--- parallel-axis-extent ---
fix(parallel): fix incorrect axis extent when any subsequent series has a larger value than the first
## Context Parallel coordinates can compute the axis extent from the first contributing series and fail to expand it for later series with larger values, causing valid data to be clipped or mis-scaled. ## Desired outcome Parallel-axis extent calculation should account for all contributing series before finalizing the displayed range. ## Acceptance signals When later series contain values outside the first series’ bounds, the parallel axis expands correctly instead of truncating the data.
--- pie-tangential-noflip ---
feat(pie): add `tangential-noflip` rotation mode to keep labels tangential without flipping
## Context Pie labels can follow the tangent of the slice, but the current tangential mode may flip labels upside down, which is undesirable for designs that prioritize stable reading orientation. ## Desired outcome Add a `label.rotate` mode named `tangential-noflip` so tangential pie labels stay aligned to the slice without flipping to the opposite reading direction. ## Acceptance signals With `label.rotate: 'tangential-noflip'`, tangential labels remain readable and tangential while avoiding the automatic upside-down flip.
--- prepublish-semicolon ---
fix: Fix missing semicolon in pre-publish.js.
## Context A small syntax mistake in the publish script is enough to derail the packaging workflow, even though there is no intended product change behind it. ## Desired outcome Repair the pre-publish tooling so the script executes cleanly and the release pipeline can proceed without altering runtime chart behavior. ## Acceptance signals Maintainers can run the publish preparation step without hitting a syntax error, and the generated chart artifacts remain otherwise unchanged.
--- radar-blur-itemstyle ---
fix(radar): itemStyle of blur not working
## Context Radar chart authors can configure blur-state styling, but `blur.itemStyle` is not actually taking effect, so blurred points keep the normal appearance instead of visually receding. ## Desired outcome Blur styling on radar series should honor the same state-specific style contract users expect elsewhere, including `blur.itemStyle` and the related line and area styling, so de-emphasized series look distinctly blurred. ## Acceptance signals When a radar series enters blur state, its symbols and associated styling follow the configured blur options instead of reusing the normal-state visuals.
--- radar-clockwise-option ---
feat(radar): add `clockwise` option
## Context Radar charts currently assume a single indicator ordering direction, which makes it awkward to match designs or domain conventions that expect the indicators to progress clockwise. ## Desired outcome Radar coordinate systems should support a `clockwise` option so authors can choose the direction in which indicators are laid out. ## Acceptance signals Setting `radar.clockwise` changes the indicator ordering direction without breaking label placement or the rest of the radar rendering contract.
--- radar-style-precedence ---
fix(radar): improve logic and add test cases of #21081
## Context After the earlier radar blur fix, state-specific radar styling can still be overridden in some interaction paths, so `emphasis.itemStyle` and blur-state styling do not always win when they should. ## Desired outcome Radar state transitions should preserve the intended style precedence so emphasis and blur visuals are applied consistently instead of being overwritten by default symbol styling. ## Acceptance signals Interacting with a radar series shows the configured emphasis and blur appearance reliably, with no cases where the point styling snaps back to an unexpected default.
--- release-6-0-0-rc1 ---
chore: release 6.0.0-rc.1
## Context The 6.0.0 release candidate needs distributable artifacts and versioned packaging that reflect the current source accurately, otherwise downstream adopters cannot validate the release in a realistic way. ## Desired outcome Prepare the 6.0.0-rc.1 release outputs and metadata so the published bundles match the release-candidate source without introducing any additional behavior changes beyond the intended release contents. ## Acceptance signals Consumers evaluating 6.0.0-rc.1 receive coherent release artifacts, version strings, and packaged outputs that line up with the release candidate they are testing.
--- release-merge-master ---
chore: merge release to master after releasing 6.0.0
## Context After cutting 6.0.0, the main branch still needs the release-side packaging and maintenance updates so future development starts from the post-release baseline rather than a partially merged state. ## Desired outcome Bring the post-release changes back onto the main line, preserving the released packaging and maintenance updates while keeping existing chart behavior unchanged. ## Acceptance signals Maintainers see the main branch aligned with the released 6.0.0 baseline, with no extra product-facing changes beyond the release merge itself.
--- seriesdata-each-example ---
chore: fix example description for the `each` method of `SeriesData`
## Context The examples for `SeriesData.each` and `DataStore.each` currently suggest a narrower usage pattern than the API actually supports, which can mislead developers reading the docs and examples. ## Desired outcome The public examples should clearly demonstrate valid iteration usage, including numeric dimension indexes, while leaving the runtime behavior unchanged. ## Acceptance signals Developers reading the examples no longer infer that only named dimensions are supported, and the API contract shown in docs matches the real behavior.
--- slider-handlelabel-optional ---
fix(type): `emphasis.handleLabel` of slider dataZoom should be an optional type
## Context TypeScript users of slider dataZoom are being told that `emphasis.handleLabel` is required even though the runtime accepts charts that omit it, creating unnecessary type errors in otherwise valid configurations. ## Desired outcome The type contract should reflect the real API by making `emphasis.handleLabel` optional for slider dataZoom. ## Acceptance signals A slider dataZoom configuration without `emphasis.handleLabel` type-checks cleanly while keeping the existing runtime behavior unchanged.
--- sunburst-root-label-centering ---
fix(sunburst): fix root node label may not be centered
## Context Sunburst root labels can drift off center in the full-circle root case, producing a visibly unbalanced chart even though the root node should act like a centered title. ## Desired outcome The root-node label should stay centered for a full-circle sunburst root, including cases where floating-point angle math would otherwise push it off center. ## Acceptance signals A sunburst with a centered root node shows the root label visually centered instead of offsetting it because of tiny angular errors.
--- time-axis-customvalues-formatter ---
fix(axis): fix chart does not work when using `customValues` with `formatter` in time axis label
## Context Time axes can break when authors combine `axisLabel.customValues` with a custom `axisLabel.formatter`, even though that pairing is a reasonable way to build bespoke label sets. ## Desired outcome Time-axis label generation should support `customValues` and formatter callbacks together without crashing or dropping the axis. ## Acceptance signals A time axis that uses both `axisLabel.customValues` and `axisLabel.formatter` renders normally and passes the formatter the expected label values.
--- toolbox-dataview-darkmode ---
fix(toolbox): fix dataView component does not fit dark mode
## Context The toolbox data view still looks like a light-theme popup when the rest of the chart is in dark mode, making the editor hard to read and visually out of place. ## Desired outcome Dark mode should style the data view surface, text, textarea, and controls coherently so the toolbox editor feels native to the dark theme. ## Acceptance signals Opening `toolbox.feature.dataView` in dark mode shows readable text and controls on an appropriate dark background instead of a mismatched light popup.
--- toolbox-emphasis-color ---
fix(toolbox): fix emphasis color to be different with default color
## Context The toolbox hover state is not visually distinct enough because the emphasis color can collapse to the default icon color, making interaction feedback easy to miss. ## Desired outcome Toolbox emphasis styling should use a different highlight color so hover and focus states are visibly distinguishable from the default icon appearance. ## Acceptance signals When the toolbox enters emphasis state, `emphasis.iconStyle.borderColor` produces a clearly different visual highlight instead of matching the normal icon color.
--- tooltip-listener-unbinding ---
fix(tooltip): fix potential memory leakage by explicitly unbinding event listeners
## Context Applications that repeatedly create and dispose tooltip-heavy charts can accumulate leftover DOM listeners, which is the kind of slow memory growth that operators only notice after long sessions or repeated route changes. ## Desired outcome Disposing or rebuilding chart tooltips should fully release the HTML tooltip event wiring so long-lived pages do not retain stale listeners or detached tooltip state. ## Acceptance signals Repeated chart teardown and recreation no longer leaves tooltip listeners behind, and tooltip behavior remains correct without introducing leaks over time.
--- typescript-esm-compatibility ---
fix(types): remove export assignment to support typescript esm compatibility
## Context TypeScript consumers using modern ESM resolution are running into friction with the published declaration entrypoints, especially in projects that mix `import` and `require` semantics. ## Desired outcome The published package should expose type entrypoints that work cleanly for modern TypeScript module resolution, including distinct ESM and CommonJS declaration paths where needed. ## Acceptance signals Projects using current TypeScript ESM rules can resolve the package’s declarations without manual hacks, and mixed consumers still receive the correct type surface for their module mode.
--- typescript-export-types ---
fix(type): fix missing or missmatched TS export types
## Context TypeScript consumers are running into missing or mismatched exported option types, especially for series that combine shared coordinate-system mixins, which makes valid configurations look unsupported in editor tooling. ## Desired outcome The published TypeScript surface should export the correct option types for affected series and include the calendar and matrix mixins where those series actually support them. ## Acceptance signals Developers importing the affected series option types no longer see missing exports or incomplete coordinate-system support in TypeScript, and valid options type-check as expected.
--- typo-cleanup ---
chore: fix typos
## Context The project has accumulated a handful of spelling mistakes and mislabeled identifiers in internal code and example data, which makes maintenance harder and leaves contributors second-guessing whether a name is intentional. ## Desired outcome Clean up the wording and identifier typos so the codebase reads consistently, while keeping existing runtime behavior, public API contracts, and chart output unchanged. ## Acceptance signals Contributors see corrected names and messages in the affected areas, and no chart behavior or user-facing option semantics change as a side effect of the cleanup.
--- validator-13-15-23 ---
chore(deps-dev): bump validator from 13.15.20 to 13.15.23
## Context The development toolchain also relies on `validator`, and the repository needs the newer 13.15.23 patch level to stay current without introducing any chart-level behavior changes. ## Desired outcome Update the pinned development dependency from `validator` 13.15.20 to 13.15.23 while keeping runtime features, output, and public APIs unchanged. ## Acceptance signals The refreshed dependency installs cleanly for contributors, and users do not observe any product-facing behavior difference from this maintenance update.
--- visualmap-darkmode-inrange ---
fix(visualMap): fix dark mode should not provide inRange
## Context In dark mode, visualMap is still injecting default `inRange` colors, which can unexpectedly override the palette choices chart authors already configured for their own mappings. ## Desired outcome The dark theme should stop supplying a default `visualMap.inRange` color mapping so dark mode does not silently change how user-defined visual mapping behaves. ## Acceptance signals Enabling dark mode no longer adds an unwanted in-range color ramp, and visualMap styling follows the user’s own configuration unless they explicitly opt in to theme values.
--- visualmap-unbounded-range ---
VisualMap support unboundedRange
## Context Continuous visual maps currently force both ends of `range` to behave as hard bounds, which makes it awkward to express common selections like “everything above this threshold” or “everything below this threshold.” ## Desired outcome Users should be able to mark one side of the selected interval as open-ended by enabling `visualMap.unboundedRange`, so the visual map can naturally represent one-sided ranges without custom workarounds. ## Acceptance signals With `visualMap.unboundedRange`, a range that touches the configured minimum or maximum behaves as an open interval on that side, while the opposite bound remains effective.
--- vue-raw-instance ---
fix(core): mark echarts instance object as raw in Vue
## Context Vue users often store the chart instance inside `ref()` or `reactive()`, but proxying the ECharts instance can interfere with instance methods and create hard-to-debug integration issues. ## Desired outcome An ECharts instance should be treated as raw when used from Vue so framework reactivity does not wrap it and break normal instance behavior. ## Acceptance signals Storing the chart instance inside Vue state no longer causes proxy-related surprises, and methods like updating options or dispatching actions keep working normally.
